The clearest ruler-attributed gain was the PACT Act, which expanded veterans’ eligibility for care related to toxic exposures and began implementation during the year; VA activity and a separate screening program also show administrative delivery and increased outpatient appointment completion. Federal gun-safety legislation and policing reforms indicate attention to public safety, although their realized welfare effects were not yet established. Against these positives, independent oversight found that only 79% of Veterans Health Administration facilities met both mental-health integration requirements, staffing constrained implementation, and VA did not centrally track or adequately oversee some nongovernmental mental-health partnerships. Inflation imposed unequal burdens, especially on lower-income households, but the dossier does not establish Biden-specific causation. The record therefore demonstrates concrete federal action and some bounded implementation, but not broad, independently verified improvement in population-wide capabilities, equity, service quality, or durable life chances. This supports a middle score rather than the 6–7 range, while the documented actions and absence of catastrophic ruler-linked deprivation reject the lower
